interest: This document provides a valuable index and high-level summary of U.S. State Department and inter-agency intelligence tracking the Imperial Japanese Navy between late 1940 and late 1943. Of particular historical significance is sub-number 123, recording an American consular observation from Nagasaki on April 18, 1941, identifying the clandestine conversion of the NYK passenger liner Kasuga Maru (later the escort carrier Taiyo) into an aircraft carrier with an unmistakable flight deck months prior to Pearl Harbor. The docket also sheds light on Axis collaboration via German nationals reconditioning and arming captured Chinese gunboats at Tsingtao, pre-war personnel recalls, and wartime intelligence collection on Japanese naval shipbuilding funneled through diplomatic missions in Ankara, Bern, and Chungking.
overview: This file consists of a two-page Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet (Form DS-46), compiled on October 12, 1945, indexing records classified under decimal file 894.30 (Japan: Naval Affairs / Naval Vessels) spanning from August 1940 through December 1943 (sub-numbers 117 to 134). The docketed entries track diplomatic reporting and military intelligence concerning Imperial Japanese Navy activities, ship conversions, personnel mobilization, and strategic capabilities prior to and during World War II. Prominent entries include assessments of naval security and commentary on Walter Lippmann columns by Stanley K. Hornbeck, reports on the mobilization of naval reservists in China, German technical involvement in reconditioning captured Chinese vessels at Tsingtao, the conversion of the liner Kasuga Maru into an aircraft carrier at Nagasaki, activity at Port Arthur, and wartime reports on Japanese naval construction from posts in Turkey, China, and Switzerland.

subfiles.about: A two-page Department of State docket sheet (Form DS-46) listing and summarizing incoming and internal communications regarding Japanese naval affairs, vessels, and personnel from August 1940 to December 1943.
subfiles.summary: This sub-file comprises the Department of State's docket list of papers (Form DS-46) for decimal file 894.30 (Naval Affairs. Naval Vessels. Japan), compiled on October 12, 1945. It catalogs sub-numbers 117 through 134, dating from August 1940 to December 1943, summarizing diplomatic cables, despatches, and memoranda between State Department divisions, overseas legations, the War and Navy Departments, and the Department of Justice. Key recorded subjects include the mobilization of naval reservists in China, German assistance in reconditioning captured Chinese vessels at Tsingtao, the conversion of the Kasuga Maru into an aircraft carrier at Nagasaki, naval officer reinstatements, and wartime intelligence on Japanese shipbuilding collected via neutral posts in Turkey and Switzerland.
